headline: Solver-blind baseline deliverable: exact projected reformulation 35,378 vars/16,516 rows -> 32,337/14,717 (3,041 columns, 1,799 rows), proved by 4 claims (forward/reverse x integer/LP) whose reverse halves are one joint IntervalLift of 930 absolute-value auxiliaries each; RPX 10,418,378 B, 525,092 obligations, 0 branches.
framework_help_in_this_run: none. The digest census 'module members touched in eval code: mps(3)' is a false positive: tools/digest_reform_run.py:159 matches identifiers m|mf|model|frame|edit|check|mipframe followed by a member; every hit is the substring 'model.mps' inside a path string. The run's 17 tool calls are 4 reads + 13 evals of hand-written Python; no mipframe call appears anywhere in the transcript.
sibling_mf_run: results.csv:22 (test30.mps, mipframe=yes, 1.0.0) reports a target of 35,378 vars/15,886 rows/122,348 nonzeros (rows -630, columns unchanged) versus the baseline row results.csv:23 at 32,337/14,717/121,057; the mf run took 27 turns, 26 tool calls, 4 failed calls and 1,177,120 tokens, the baseline 18 turns, 17 calls, 0 failures and 346,857 tokens. No runs/test30-mf-B1 directory survives on disk, so the row is the only evidence. So the framework-assisted sibling delivered a row-only reduction while the baseline had to find every column elimination, every auxiliary family and every certificate itself (all 13 evals are custom parsing, census, regeneration and boundary testing).
claims: Four claims in cases/test30/request.json: {forward,reverse} x {input_integers=output_integers=True/False}, objective 'Equal', inverse None, projection = 32,337 retained [source,target] pairs (counts.claims=4 in cases/test30/preparation.json).

Reformulation keeps the same feasible projection onto retained variables and the same objective for the integer model and for the LP relaxation; it is a size reduction, not an LP strengthening (digest final report; cases/test30/README.md).

Content: 930 free auxiliaries a=|d| (rows d-a<=0, -d-a<=0, u-a>=b) replaced by u-d>=b and u+d>=b; 31 nonnegative auxiliaries (u-a>=b, a>=0) replaced by u>=b with a=0; 620 alias binaries (31 classes of 21) collapsed to lexicographic representatives; 1,460 private binaries projected out of 640 sum-to-binary equalities; 220 box-implied rows and 29 duplicate copies dropped (cases/test30/preparation.json counts).
proof_encoding: proof.rpa = 'RPA 5' + one JSON certificate, 16,302,197 B: 8 blocks (4 claims, forward block = Lin steps + Return, reverse block = IntervalLift{intervals:[930 x {lower,upper,checks}],body:{steps,Return}}); proof.rpx 10,418,378 B, 525,092 obligations, 6,663,662 work units, 0 branches (cases/test30/README.md; preparation.json).

Verify statistics (cases/test30/preparation.json kernel_runs[3]): interval_lifts 2, interval_generated_variables 1,860, interval_generated_rows 5,580, interval_generated_terms 17,720, linear_terms 80,332, peak_live_facts 3,552, bijections 0, points 0, exit 0, execute_us 172,759.

Forward blocks: one Lin fact per target row (the 930 added Q rows use the row combination [RowUpper,RowLower] at prepare_test30.py:49, the 640 projected rows use the source equality plus one VarLower per removed private binary at :83), alias equality facts per removed alias, VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt checks, and 32,337 'Exact' padding entries per claim (:117).
Reverse blocks: Box facts for bound checks, RowUpper/RowLower refs into the IntervalLift layout for the 2,821 source rows touched by auxiliaries, 'Exact' where the dependency vanishes (:100-116).
Budgets: verify ran with the recorded command and no --work flag; RPA 16.3 MB and request 1.69 MB are far below the 256 MiB text limit, so no multi-part assembly was needed.
agent_manual_work: Whole-file MPS interpretation written twice by hand: a token reader using Fraction per decimal token and an independently implemented fixed-position reader using Decimal, forced to agree on every row sense, coefficient, RHS, bound, integrality flag and objective coefficient (digest evals 'Parsing exact MPS data' and 'Independently auditing representation and algebra'; report section 'MPS interpretation and evidence reliability').

Structural census by hand: row-signature grouping, continuous participation, incidence degrees, singleton columns, binary equality aliases, duplicate rows, and a union-find incidence graph that returned one component of all 35,378 columns (digest evals 3-6).

Its own oracle: regenerated all 14,718 final rows from original row combinations plus alias maps plus singleton removal sets, plus 2,200 exhaustive local binary truth tables, 4,440 fractional reconstruction cases and 14,043 rational auxiliary boundary scenarios (digest eval 'Independent auditing representation and algebra' and 'Exercising projected behaviour'; audit.json.verification).

Wrote the reformulated MPS (4,283,495 B) and a 3,579,179 B audit.json with reconstruction maps plus 5,661 row-diff records, then round-tripped the written file through the independent reader (digest eval 'Writing and independently checking final artifact').

Rejected hypotheses had to be tested and reported: one-singleton-per-row (falsified by multiplicity 380/220/40) and all-31-free-columns-have-definitions (falsified by C0083..C0093) (digest final report, section 5 and 6).
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test30.py is 144 lines and imports six sibling modules: parse_mps,row_ref (prepare_affine), expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,sha (prepare_test40), substitute (prepare_test57), fact,box,exact (prepare_test54), SparseBuilder (prepare_test70), extend (prepare_test23).
Hand-rolled exact linear algebra on dicts {var index: Fraction}: expression/plus/mul/substitute/exact plus the wire encoder expr_json -> {'constant','terms':[[i,'p/q']]}.

Hand-rolled RPA emission: SparseBuilder.lin() appends {'Lin':{id,kind,constant,terms}} and asserts the residual against the Python expression; fact() collapses to 'Exact'; box() emits VarLower/VarUpper terms; Return/IntervalLift bodies are assembled as raw dicts (tools/prepare_test70.py:20-31, tools/prepare_test54.py:16-33).

Hand-rolled audit ingress: h['alias_eliminations'].column_to_representative / removed_equality_rows, h['auxiliary_eliminations'][].upper_row/lower_rows, h['singleton_eliminations'][].removed_variables, h['duplicate_row_removals'] are re-keyed by name, and the resulting target boundary is only checked by an ad-hoc set equality (prepare_test30.py:16-18,27).

extend() (tools/prepare_test23.py:15-29) deep-copies the target model, appends one free real 'interval_k' variable and one generated row per interval endpoint, renumbers rows, and returns the layout that the reverse block's RowUpper/RowLower refs point at.
friction: request.json is 1,731,787 B and 1,731,336 B of it (99.97%) is the projection: four copies of the same 32,337-pair array (claims 0==2 and 1==3; claim 1 is exactly claim 0 with each pair's components swapped).

The retained coordinate set is the source minus exactly 3,041 indices, i.e. 143 contiguous exclusion ranges serialising to 1,877 B; a claim carrying those ranges instead of the pair list serialises to 2,034 B, so the caller contract is roughly 850x larger than it needs to be.

The target model is never constructed from the audit's edits: preparation.json kernel_runs[1] is a second 'rpx canonical' over the analyst's output/reformulated.mps, so proof and model can drift; the only guard is the preparer's ad-hoc assertion that removed columns equal source vars absent from the target.

129,348 of the 525,092 obligations are the padding entries checks.extend(['Exact']*len(common)) written by hand at prepare_test30.py:117 (32,337 per claim), i.e. one empty obligation per retained coordinate per claim.

The four mutation proofs are produced by structural search over raw RPA JSON (next(Lin step of kind Eq with >1 terms).terms.pop(), etc.) at prepare_test30.py:134-137, with the rejection reported as an obligation index such as 'obligation 96826' and no name map back to the step.
